comparison: Both address claims C75-C76 about temporal stability of cell states (within-cell vs between-cell variability). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by Figure 2—figure supplement 7, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting the data should be moved to main text and that within-cell variability estimates need revision as 'the true variability is clearly larger than previously assumed.'

Both evaluate claims C7, C24, C29, C77, C85, C116 about cell state variables correlating with sensing abilities (Figure 3). Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes quantitative support from correlation coefficients, and peer reviewers acknowledge this finding without raising concerns.

Both address claims C30, C86-C96 about cell state dynamics and timescale effects (Figure 4). Both rate these claims as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes how the model demonstrates timescale separation effects, and peer reviewers accept this theoretical analysis without critique.

Both evaluate experimental validation claims (C6, C28, C70, C72) and C74. OpenEval rates these SUPPORTED, emphasizing the close match between experimental and computational distributions as 'critical validation.' Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with concerns about within-cell variability underestimation, model dependency, and that information quantities (~2 bits) merely reflect the small number of tested doses rather than approaching information capacity.

Both address forward-looking claims C105-C109 about potential applications. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting these are 'largely speculative statements' about proposed rather than demonstrated applications. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, with no challenges to these future utility statements, focusing concerns elsewhere on current data analysis.

Both evaluate main computational findings (C4-C5, C26-C27, C61, C63, C73). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with caveat about model-dependent uncertainty. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with critical concerns about within-cell variability magnitude, lack of revision to information estimates, and that for EGF/EGFR 'the system does not have any data to support any claim about single-cell information that's not heavily informed by models.'

Both address toy model analysis claims C25, C45-C47. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting the mathematical proof and effective demonstration. Peer reviewer sa0 supports the work 'convincingly highlights the difference,' though sa1 raises broader concerns about variability estimates that affect interpretation of the overall findings including the toy model context.

Both address methodological framework claims C22, C35 (and R6 includes C104, C117). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting sound theoretical foundation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, with sa0 describing effective use of the framework and sa2 supporting the utility of conditional mutual information metric, though concerns exist about specific data analysis choices.

Partial overlap on conclusion claims C101, C114-C115. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing successful bridging of computational and experimental approaches. Peer reviewers rate the broader set UNCERTAIN due to concerns about within-cell variability and model dependency affecting the strength of conclusions.

OpenEval evaluates foundational information theory definitions (C1, C9, C10) as SUPPORTED, noting these are well-established concepts from standard literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates literature summary claims (C2, C12-C16) as SUPPORTED, noting accurate characterization of prior work with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates claims about cell state heterogeneity (C3, C17-C20) as SUPPORTED, noting well-founded hypothesis derived from multiple citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates modeling approach claims (C48-C49, C54-C55, C57-C59) as SUPPORTED with caveat that accurate fit claim would benefit from quantitative goodness-of-fit metrics. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates claim C34 as SUPPORTED, noting it is a direct mathematical consequence of proven inequality. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic interpretation claims (C97-C98, C110-C111, C113) as SUPPORTED, noting conceptually sound explanations with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates claims about experimental limitations (C102-C103) as SUPPORTED, noting these are well-recognized constraints motivating computational approaches. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates IGF/FoxO pathway biology claims (C50-C52) as SUPPORTED, noting well-characterized features with appropriate citation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates claim C11 about channel capacity analysis applications as SUPPORTED with citations to previous work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
